title: Grounds for Dissolution of Marriage by a Muslim Woman — Section 2 DMMA

content.overview: Section 2 of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 enables a Muslim woman to obtain a decree of dissolution of marriage on specified statutory grounds, including the husband’s disappearance, failure to provide maintenance, imprisonment, failure to perform marital obligations, impotence, specified diseases or conditions, cruelty, and other grounds recognized under Muslim law as enacted.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Muslim wife petitioner? (2) Which s. 2 ground? (3) Ingredients proved? (4) Decree of dissolution sought?
content.study:
DMMA gives the wife a statutory path to judicial dissolution. Each ground has its own ingredients and must be proved.

Case already in migrated file: Shamim Ara v. State of U.P. (2002) 7 SCC 518 — a bare assertion of talaq is not sufficient; the factum and legal validity of talaq must be established in accordance with law. Relevant when talaq is pleaded as a related issue. No additional cases invented.

sections.heading: Statutory grounds
sections.body: Disappearance; non-maintenance; imprisonment; failure of marital obligations; impotence; specified conditions; cruelty; other recognized Muslim-law grounds as enacted.

sections.heading: Proof
sections.body: Each ground must be established on the facts; pleadings and evidence must match the statutory head relied on.

sections.heading: Relief
sections.body: Decree of dissolution of marriage under the Act.

sections.heading: Relation to talaq issues
sections.body: Where talaq is asserted, factum and validity must be proved; bare assertion is insufficient (Shamim Ara).

provisions.title: Grounds for decree for dissolution of marriage

examples.title: Non-maintenance ground
examples.body: Wife proves husband has failed to provide maintenance for the statutory period — may seek dissolution under the corresponding s. 2 head.

hypotheticals.question: Is a bare claim of talaq enough to end the marriage without proof?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Shamim Ara requires the factum and legal validity of talaq to be established in accordance with law.

distinctions.title: DMMA judicial dissolution vs unilateral talaq claims
distinctions.left: Wife’s statutory petition on s. 2 grounds.
distinctions.right: Husband’s claimed talaq — factum and validity must be proved.

rows.right: Proof of valid talaq if relied on.

misconceptions.trap: Any marital grievance automatically attracts s. 2.
misconceptions.correction: The specific statutory ground and its ingredients must be pleaded and proved.
